review_note: Keep the four-part method, worked entry, unrestricted length and marking rules. Cut the brief praising its own policy and the unsupported claim that word limits cause AI submissions.

edits.before:
**Your best ten count**, so one week is yours to drop. That's deliberate. A
course that teaches masking as a budget, and then punishes one overspent week,
isn't taking its own week 6 seriously.
edits.after: **Your best ten count**, so one week is yours to drop.
edits.reason: The drop rule is useful; announcing that it proves the course takes itself seriously adds no instruction.

edits.before:
> **The rule now.** Held, with an addition: the pause means *not in front of
> the group*. Ask again, privately, with an explicit exit.
edits.after:
> **The rule now.** Revised: a delayed yes is a reason to check availability
> again, with an explicit exit. This test does not tell me whether being in
> front of the group caused the pause.
edits.reason: The fictional test establishes a different preferred day, not why the person paused. Model a revision that reports that limit instead of treating the audience explanation as confirmed.
